title: The delivery kit: the demo that doesn't depend on the client's wifi
pitch: You build the complete package an AI project gets delivered with: a README that makes sense, a three-minute demo that works with the phone in airplane mode, a case study with hours and euros actually measured, and a proposal with scope, price, and what it does NOT include. This is what separates someone who "knows AI" from someone who gets paid for it.
outcome: A compressed folder under 100 kB you can send to a client or show in an interview. Inside: code that works without internet, a report with 11 out of 12 correct on real measurements, and a €900 proposal that justifies itself with €143.94 in monthly savings.
requires: Python 3.11 or higher. Check by typing `python --version` in the terminal.
An open terminal: PowerShell on Windows, Terminal on Mac or Linux.
Knowing how to create a folder and move around it from the terminal. `mkdir` and `cd` are enough; step 1 walks you through it.

Anthropic API key: OPTIONAL. The whole project starts and works without a key and without spending a euro. You only need it if you want to re-record the answers with the real model, and that costs less than a cent.

structure.what: Every number in the project in a single place: client, email volume, rates, price. If a number appears in two places, sooner or later one of them will be wrong.
Writes correos.csv (12 real anonymized emails with the correct category next to each) and the 12 sample recordings. It's the classifier's exam.
The product. Labels an email. Two modes: record (calls the model, spends money) and replay (reads from grabaciones/, free and offline).
The three-minute demo. Runs in front of the client and never touches the internet.
Measures real accuracy over the 12 emails and translates it into hours and euros. Writes cifras.json.
Generates PROPUESTA.md: scope, what it does NOT include, price, timeline, data protection, and terms.
The dress rehearsal. Cuts the network on purpose and checks seven things before the client does.
Writes the README with the measured figures inside, creates the .gitignore, and builds entrega.zip.

steps.title: Set up the folder and keep the key out of sight
steps.why: A virtual environment is a separate box where this project's libraries live, and only this project's. Without it, you install things that clash between projects. And the API key goes into an environment variable (a value that lives in the terminal window, not in a file) because files get copied, pushed to GitHub, and emailed around. The key doesn't.
steps.code:
# All of this is typed into the terminal. The active lines are for Windows
# (PowerShell). If you're on Mac or Linux, use the commented ones below.

# 1. Project folder
mkdir maletin-entrega
cd maletin-entrega

# 2. Virtual environment: a separate box where THIS project's libraries
#    live, so they don't mix with other projects'. Created once.
python -m venv .venv

# 3. Activate the box. When it works, (.venv) shows up at the start of the line.
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# Mac or Linux:  source .venv/bin/activate

# 4. The project's only library. Only used when you RECORD new model
#    answers. The demo works without it.
pip install anthropic

# 5. The API key, only if you have one. Never written inside a project
#    file: files get copied, pushed, and emailed.
#    This line only lasts while this window is open.
$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "paste-your-key-here"
# Mac or Linux:  export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="paste-your-key-here"

# 6. Check
python --version
steps.expected: The terminal line shows `(.venv)` at the start, `pip install anthropic` finishes with "Successfully installed anthropic…" and `python --version` answers something like `Python 3.12.4`.
steps.trouble: On Windows, `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` can give "cannot load the file… running scripts is disabled". Type `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass` and activate it again. `-Scope Process` matters: it only affects this window and disappears when you close it.

steps.title: datos.json: every number in one file
steps.why: The classic delivery mistake: the README says 12 hours saved, the proposal says 10, and in the meeting you say 14. Credibility gone. Here every number lives in exactly one place and everything else reads it from there. Change 420 to 600 and the whole proposal recalculates itself.
steps.expected: A `datos.json` file inside `maletin-entrega`. Check it with `python -c "import json;print(json.load(open('datos.json',encoding='utf-8'))['cliente'])"`: it answers `Gestoría Arriaga (Zaragoza, 3 people)`.
steps.trouble: "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes" means you left a trailing comma before a `}` or added a comment. JSON allows neither dangling commas nor comments. Remove the extra comma and you're set.

steps.title: clasifica.py: the product, with record mode and replay mode
steps.why: This is the trick that saves the demo. Each email turns into a fingerprint (a short, unique text computed from the email). If a file with that fingerprint exists in `grabaciones/`, that answer gets used: zero network, zero euros, identical result every time. If it doesn't exist and you pass `--grabar`, it calls the model and saves it. The API library gets imported inside that branch on purpose: in demo mode it never even loads.
steps.code:
# clasifica.py — the product you're selling.
'''Labels a customer email.

Two modes:
  - replay (default): the answer comes from grabaciones/. No internet
    and no cost. This is the mode you use for the demo.
  - record (--grabar): really calls the model and saves the answer.

The key NEVER gets written here. It comes from the environment variable.
'''
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent
GRABACIONES = AQUI / "grabaciones"
CATEGORIAS = ["nomina", "factura", "impuesto", "cita", "otros"]

INSTRUCCION = (
    "You are the email classifier for an accounting firm. Read the email and reply "
    "ONLY with one word from this list: " + ", ".join(CATEGORIAS) + ". "
    "Nothing else: no period, no explanation, no greeting."
)


def datos():
    '''All the project's numbers live in a single file.'''
    return json.loads((AQUI / "datos.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def clave(texto, modelo):
    '''Fingerprint of the (model, email) pair. The same email always gives the
    same fingerprint, so it always finds its recording. Change a comma in
    the email and the fingerprint changes and the recording stops matching.'''
    crudo = modelo + "\n" + texto.strip()
    return hashlib.sha1(crudo.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def clasifica(texto, modelo, grabar=False):
    GRABACIONES.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    fichero = GRABACIONES / (clave(texto, modelo) + ".json")

    # Replay mode: read from disk and exit. No network here whatsoever.
    if fichero.exists() and not grabar:
        guardado = json.loads(fichero.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        guardado["origen"] = "grabacion"
        return guardado

    if not grabar:
        raise SystemExit(
            "No recording for this email (" + fichero.name + ").\n"
            "Fix A: run  python siembra.py  for the example recordings.\n"
            "Fix B: run with --grabar and a key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY."
        )

    api_key = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise SystemExit(
            "Missing environment variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.\n"
            "Don't paste the key into the code: the code gets shared, the key doesn't."
        )

    # The import goes in here on purpose: in demo mode this library never
    # even loads, so the demo can't touch the network by accident.
    from anthropic import Anthropic

    cliente = Anthropic(api_key=api_key)
    respuesta = cliente.messages.create(
        model=modelo,
        max_tokens=10,
        system=INSTRUCCION,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": texto}],
    )
    cruda = respuesta.content[0].text.strip().lower()
    salida = {
        "categoria": cruda if cruda in CATEGORIAS else "otros",
        "cruda": cruda,
        "tokens_entrada": respuesta.usage.input_tokens,
        "tokens_salida": respuesta.usage.output_tokens,
    }
    fichero.write_text(json.dumps(salida, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    salida["origen"] = "api"
    return salida


if __name__ == "__main__":
    grabar = "--grabar" in sys.argv
    trozos = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--grabar"]
    if not trozos:
        raise SystemExit('Usage: python clasifica.py "email text" [--grabar]')
    resultado = clasifica(" ".join(trozos), datos()["modelo"], grabar=grabar)
    print(resultado["categoria"] + "   (source: " + resultado["origen"] + ")")
steps.expected: Run `python clasifica.py "here's May's invoice"`. You'll see the message: "No recording for this email (…json). Fix A: run python siembra.py…". That's exactly what you want to see: an error that explains itself and tells you what to do.
steps.trouble: If you use `--grabar` and get `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'anthropic'`, your environment isn't activated. Check for `(.venv)` at the start of the line; if not, go back to step 1 and activate it.

steps.title: siembra.py: the 12 exam emails and their recordings
steps.why: No data, no demo, no accuracy figure. These 12 emails are from a real accounting firm, anonymized: names changed, amounts changed, phone numbers truncated. Anonymizing isn't a courtesy, it's a legal requirement. And one of the 12 gets misclassified on purpose: no client who's ever worked with software believes a case study with 12 out of 12.
steps.code:
# siembra.py — creates the classifier's exam and its 12 recordings.
'''Writes correos.csv and the 12 example recordings.

The recordings come pre-made so the project starts with no key and no cost.
Once you have a key: delete the grabaciones/ folder and re-record with
python clasifica.py "..." --grabar to get real answers.
'''
import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from clasifica import clave, datos

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent
GRABACIONES = AQUI / "grabaciones"

# (email text, correct category, what the model answers, input tokens)
# Real accounting-firm data, anonymized: names changed, amounts changed,
# phone numbers truncated. This isn't optional, it's the law.
CORREOS = [
    ("Good morning. Could you send me Rocio's May payslip, the girl in admin? The bank is asking for it for the store loan and they want it as a signed PDF. Today if possible, they need it before Friday. Thanks.",
     "nomina", "nomina", 168),
    ("Hi, attaching this month's invoice from Suministros Belmar, 1,240.50 EUR with VAT. It's the office supplies one I mentioned on the phone. Confirm it arrived okay because last month it stayed a draft.",
     "factura", "factura", 142),
    ("A question: is Q2 form 303 due July 20th or do I have until end of month? I've been told different things and I don't want a repeat of last year's surcharge.",
     "impuesto", "impuesto", 155),
    ("Do you have a slot Thursday afternoon to review the half-year close? I'm free from 17:00 and it would help if whoever handles payroll could join too. An hour should be plenty, I think.",
     "cita", "cita", 149),
    ("Good afternoon. I've changed phones and the old number no longer works. The new one ends in 412, note it down for when you need to call me. Everything else stays the same, same email as always.",
     "otros", "otros", 131),
    ("Going through the quarterly summary I see an invoice is missing: the October one from Talleres Nadal, 480 EUR without VAT. I'm sure I sent it because I mailed it together with the MOT one. Can you check?",
     "factura", "factura", 160),
    ("I need to onboard a new person starting June 1st, 20-hour weekly contract Monday to Friday mornings. They're 24 and it's their first job. Tell me what paperwork you need from me.",
     "nomina", "nomina", 176),
    ("I got a notice from the tax office about 2024 income tax, I think it's about rental withholdings. I'll forward it once I scan it. Is this serious or the kind of notice you just reply to and it's done?",
     "impuesto", "impuesto", 138),
    ("Can we move Tuesday's meeting to Wednesday same time? A warehouse visit came up that I can't reschedule. If Wednesday doesn't work for you, tell me what day you're free.",
     "cita", "cita", 121),
    ("Thanks so much for the other day, everything worked out and the bank guy didn't make a fuss. You're great. Have a good weekend, talk next week.",
     "otros", "otros", 118),
    # This is the classifier's mistake, and it stays that way. A case study
    # with no mistakes convinces nobody.
    ("Can you confirm you got the 14 invoices I uploaded yesterday to the shared folder? I uploaded them around nine at night and got no confirmation, so I don't know if they went through halfway.",
     "factura", "otros", 152),
    ("Attaching the rental withholding certificate for the storefront for the income tax return. Same landlord as last year, so I assume you already have their details. Let me know if anything else is needed.",
     "impuesto", "impuesto", 145),
]


def main():
    forzar = "--forzar" in sys.argv
    modelo = datos()["modelo"]
    GRABACIONES.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    with (AQUI / "correos.csv").open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        escritor = csv.writer(f)
        escritor.writerow(["id", "texto", "categoria"])
        for i, (texto, correcta, _, _) in enumerate(CORREOS, 1):
            escritor.writerow([i, texto, correcta])

    nuevas = saltadas = 0
    for texto, _, respuesta_modelo, tokens_in in CORREOS:
        fichero = GRABACIONES / (clave(texto, modelo) + ".json")
        if fichero.exists() and not forzar:
            saltadas += 1
            continue
        fichero.write_text(json.dumps({
            "categoria": respuesta_modelo,
            "cruda": respuesta_modelo,
            "tokens_entrada": tokens_in,
            "tokens_salida": 3,
        }, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        nuevas += 1

    print("correos.csv written: " + str(len(CORREOS)) + " emails")
    print("recordings: " + str(nuevas) + " new, " + str(saltadas) + " already existed")
    print("Note: these recordings are examples. With a key, delete grabaciones/ and re-record.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: `python siembra.py` answers: "correos.csv written: 12 emails", "recordings: 12 new, 0 already existed" and the note that these are example recordings. A `grabaciones` folder appears with 12 `.json` files.
steps.trouble: `ImportError: cannot import name 'clave' from 'clasifica'` means you're running from outside the folder or the file from step 3 is named differently. Go in with `cd maletin-entrega` and check `clasifica.py` exists with `dir` (Windows) or `ls` (Mac/Linux).

steps.title: demo.py: three minutes in front of the client, no network
steps.why: Demo day has two scenarios: the room's wifi doesn't work, or the model takes eight seconds per email and the client stares at the ceiling. Both get fixed the same way: the demo reads from the recordings. It comes out the same every time, takes four seconds, and works on a train. The 0.35 s pause isn't decoration: it gives you time to read each line while you talk.
steps.code:
# demo.py — what you run in front of the client.
'''Classifies the 12 emails in correos.csv and shows the table.

Doesn't touch the internet. Every answer comes from grabaciones/. With --rapido
it runs with no pauses (used by verifica.py).
'''
import csv
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from clasifica import clasifica, datos

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent
ANCHO = 46


def corta(texto):
    if len(texto) <= ANCHO:
        return texto
    return texto[:ANCHO - 3] + "..."


def coma(numero, decimales=1):
    '''In Spain decimals use a comma. A two-line detail that keeps
    the demo from looking imported.'''
    return ("{:." + str(decimales) + "f}").format(numero).replace(".", ",")


def main():
    rapido = "--rapido" in sys.argv
    d = datos()
    with (AQUI / "correos.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        filas = list(csv.DictReader(f))

    print("")
    print("DEMO - Incoming email classifier")
    print("Client: " + d["cliente"])
    print(str(len(filas)) + " real, anonymized emails. No internet: everything comes from grabaciones/.")
    print("")
    print("{:>2}  {:<46}  {:<9} {:<9}".format("#", "Email", "Predicted", "Correct"))
    print("-" * 77)

    aciertos = 0
    tokens_in = 0
    tokens_out = 0
    inicio = time.time()

    for i, fila in enumerate(filas, 1):
        r = clasifica(fila["texto"], d["modelo"])
        bien = r["categoria"] == fila["categoria"]
        if bien:
            aciertos += 1
        tokens_in += r["tokens_entrada"]
        tokens_out += r["tokens_salida"]
        print("{:>2}  {:<46}  {:<9} {:<9} {}".format(
            i, corta(fila["texto"]), r["categoria"], fila["categoria"],
            "OK" if bien else "MISS"))
        if not rapido:
            time.sleep(0.35)

    coste = (tokens_in / 1e6) * d["eur_por_millon_entrada"] + \
            (tokens_out / 1e6) * d["eur_por_millon_salida"]

    print("-" * 77)
    print("Correct: " + str(aciertos) + " of " + str(len(filas)) +
          "  (" + coma(100 * aciertos / len(filas)) + " %)")
    print("Real cost of these " + str(len(filas)) + " emails: " + coma(coste, 4) + " EUR")
    print("Duration: " + coma(time.time() - inicio) + " s. Zero internet requests.")
    print("")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: A 12-row table. Row 11 says MISS (it predicts `otros`, the correct one is `factura`). At the end: "Correct: 11 of 12  (91,7 %)", "Real cost of these 12 emails: 0,0017 EUR" and "Duration: 4,2 s. Zero internet requests."
steps.trouble: If it says "No recording for this email", you changed an email's text after seeding. The fingerprint is computed from the text: change a comma and it can't find its recording anymore. Run `python siembra.py --forzar` to regenerate them.

steps.title: cifras.py: turn accuracy into hours and euros
steps.why: "91.7% accurate" doesn't tell whoever's signing anything. "Gives you back 10.5 hours a month" does. And there's a subtraction almost nobody does: the classifier's own mistakes also cost time to fix, about 35 emails a month. That time gets subtracted right here. A case study that doesn't subtract its own mistakes is advertising.
steps.code:
# cifras.py — turns accuracy into hours and euros.
'''Measures accuracy over correos.csv, translates it into money, and writes cifras.json.

Also counts the cost of fixing the classifier's own mistakes. A case study that
doesn't subtract its mistakes is advertising, not a case study.
'''
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

from clasifica import clasifica, datos

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent


def coma(numero, decimales=2):
    return ("{:." + str(decimales) + "f}").format(numero).replace(".", ",")


def main():
    d = datos()
    with (AQUI / "correos.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        filas = list(csv.DictReader(f))

    aciertos = 0
    tokens_in = 0
    tokens_out = 0
    for fila in filas:
        r = clasifica(fila["texto"], d["modelo"])
        if r["categoria"] == fila["categoria"]:
            aciertos += 1
        tokens_in += r["tokens_entrada"]
        tokens_out += r["tokens_salida"]

    n = len(filas)
    acierto = aciertos / n
    media_in = tokens_in / n
    media_out = tokens_out / n

    correos = d["correos_al_mes"]
    horas_mano = correos * d["minutos_a_mano_por_correo"] / 60
    horas_revision = correos * d["segundos_revision_por_correo"] / 3600
    fallos_mes = correos * (1 - acierto)
    horas_arreglar = fallos_mes * d["minutos_corregir_un_fallo"] / 60
    horas_con = horas_revision + horas_arreglar
    horas_ahorradas = horas_mano - horas_con

    ahorro_bruto = horas_ahorradas * d["coste_hora_admin_eur"]
    coste_api = (correos * media_in / 1e6) * d["eur_por_millon_entrada"] + \
                (correos * media_out / 1e6) * d["eur_por_millon_salida"]
    ahorro_neto = ahorro_bruto - coste_api - d["precio_mantenimiento_mes_eur"]
    retorno = d["precio_implantacion_eur"] / ahorro_neto if ahorro_neto > 0 else 0
    primer_ano = ahorro_neto * 12 - d["precio_implantacion_eur"]

    cifras = {
        "correos_probados": n,
        "aciertos": aciertos,
        "acierto": round(acierto, 4),
        "media_tokens_entrada": round(media_in, 1),
        "media_tokens_salida": round(media_out, 1),
        "horas_a_mano_mes": round(horas_mano, 2),
        "horas_revision_mes": round(horas_revision, 2),
        "horas_arreglar_fallos_mes": round(horas_arreglar, 2),
        "horas_con_herramienta_mes": round(horas_con, 2),
        "horas_ahorradas_mes": round(horas_ahorradas, 2),
        "ahorro_bruto_mes_eur": round(ahorro_bruto, 2),
        "coste_api_mes_eur": round(coste_api, 2),
        "ahorro_neto_mes_eur": round(ahorro_neto, 2),
        "meses_retorno": round(retorno, 1),
        "ahorro_primer_ano_eur": round(primer_ano, 2),
    }
    (AQUI / "cifras.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(cifras, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print("")
    print("MEASURED FIGURES - " + d["cliente"])
    print("")
    print("Accuracy over " + str(n) + " hand-labeled emails: " +
          str(aciertos) + " = " + coma(100 * acierto, 1) + " %")
    print("Tokens per email (measured): " + coma(media_in, 1) + " input, " +
          coma(media_out, 1) + " output")
    print("")
    print("By hand:             " + coma(horas_mano, 1) + " h/month")
    print("With the tool:       " + coma(horas_con, 1) + " h/month  (" +
          coma(horas_revision, 1) + " reviewing + " + coma(horas_arreglar, 1) + " fixing mistakes)")
    print("Savings:             " + coma(horas_ahorradas, 1) + " h/month = " +
          coma(ahorro_bruto) + " EUR")
    print("")
    print("AI bill:             " + coma(coste_api) + " EUR/month")
    print("Maintenance:         " + coma(d["precio_mantenimiento_mes_eur"]) + " EUR/month")
    print("Net savings:         " + coma(ahorro_neto) + " EUR/month")
    print("")
    print("The implementation (" + coma(d["precio_implantacion_eur"]) +
          " EUR) pays for itself in " + coma(retorno, 1) + " months.")
    print("First year: " + coma(primer_ano) + " EUR in the client's favor.")
    print("")
    print("Written: cifras.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: You'll see: accuracy 91.7%, "By hand: 14.0 h/month", "With the tool: 3.5 h/month (2.3 reviewing + 1.2 fixing mistakes)", "Net savings: 143.94 EUR/month" and "pays for itself in 6.3 months". `cifras.json` gets created.
steps.trouble: `KeyError: 'coste_hora_admin_eur'` means `datos.json` is missing that key: you probably deleted it while editing. Compare your file to step 2's, key by key.

steps.title: propuesta.py: scope, price, and what it does NOT include
steps.why: Proposals don't get lost over being expensive, they get lost over being ambiguous. The section that decides it is "What it does NOT include": leave it out and the client will assume you're also connecting their accounting software, and two months in you'll be working for free. And not a single number gets typed here: they come from datos.json and cifras.json.
steps.code:
# propuesta.py — generates PROPUESTA.md with the real figures inside.
'''Combines datos.json (what you decide) with cifras.json (what you measured).

No number is written by hand here. If a number changes, it changes in one place.
'''
import json
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent


def coma(numero, decimales=2):
    return ("{:." + str(decimales) + "f}").format(numero).replace(".", ",")


def main():
    d = json.loads((AQUI / "datos.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    fichero_cifras = AQUI / "cifras.json"
    if not fichero_cifras.exists():
        raise SystemExit("Missing cifras.json. Run first:  python cifras.py")
    c = json.loads(fichero_cifras.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    hoy = date.today()
    caduca = hoy + timedelta(days=d["validez_oferta_dias"])

    texto = rf'''# Proposal: incoming email classifier

**To:** {d["contacto"]} - {d["cliente"]}
**Date:** {hoy.isoformat()}
**Valid until:** {caduca.isoformat()}

## The problem, in numbers

{d["correos_al_mes"]} customer emails come in every month. Classifying them by hand costs
{coma(d["minutos_a_mano_por_correo"], 1)} minutes each: **{coma(c["horas_a_mano_mes"], 1)} hours a month** for someone
who earns {coma(d["coste_hora_admin_eur"])} EUR an hour.

## What I deliver

1. A classifier that labels every incoming email as payroll, invoice,
   tax, meeting, or other.
2. A demo that works without internet, so you can show it to your team
   whenever you want without depending on anyone.
3. A monthly report with **measured** accuracy, not estimated.
4. A 90-minute training session with the three people at the firm.

## What it does NOT include

- It doesn't reply to emails. It only labels them.
- It doesn't connect to your accounting software or document manager.
  That's a separate project and gets quoted separately.
- It doesn't read attachments. If the information is only inside an
  attached PDF, the email falls into "other".
- It does not guarantee 100%. Read the next section.

## What I promise and how it's measured

Over {c["correos_probados"]} of your own hand-labeled emails it gets {c["aciertos"]} right: {coma(100 * c["acierto"], 1)} %.

steps.title: verifica.py: cut the network on purpose and see if it holds
steps.why: "It worked on my computer" is the sentence that sinks a demo. This check swaps out the function Python uses to open connections for one that blows up, and runs the demo that way. If anything tried to reach the internet, it explodes here, at your desk, not in front of the client. The other six checks look at the usual things: missing numbers, unfilled blanks, and forgotten keys inside a file.
steps.code:
# verifica.py — the dress rehearsal before sitting down with the client.
'''Seven checks. If all seven pass, the package is ready to show.

Number 4 is the important one: it really cuts the network and runs the demo. If
the demo tries to reach the internet, it blows up here and not in front of the client.
'''
import contextlib
import csv
import io
import json
import runpy
import socket
import sys
from pathlib import Path

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent
CATEGORIAS = {"nomina", "factura", "impuesto", "cita", "otros"}
CLAVES = [
    "cliente", "contacto", "modelo", "correos_al_mes",
    "minutos_a_mano_por_correo", "segundos_revision_por_correo",
    "minutos_corregir_un_fallo", "coste_hora_admin_eur",
    "eur_por_millon_entrada", "eur_por_millon_salida",
    "precio_implantacion_eur", "precio_mantenimiento_mes_eur",
    "acierto_prometido", "correos_de_prueba_cliente", "plazo_semanas",
    "validez_oferta_dias",
]
resultados = []


def apunta(ok, texto):
    resultados.append((ok, texto))


def sin_red(*args, **kwargs):
    raise OSError("The demo tried to reach the internet.")


def prueba_1_datos():
    d = json.loads((AQUI / "datos.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    faltan = [k for k in CLAVES if k not in d]
    apunta(not faltan, "datos.json complete (" + str(len(CLAVES)) + " keys)"
           if not faltan else "datos.json: missing keys -> " + ", ".join(faltan))
    return d


def prueba_2_correos():
    with (AQUI / "correos.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        filas = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    malas = [f["categoria"] for f in filas if f["categoria"] not in CATEGORIAS]
    ok = len(filas) >= 10 and not malas
    apunta(ok, "correos.csv: " + str(len(filas)) + " rows, valid categories"
           if ok else "correos.csv: " + str(len(filas)) + " rows, odd categories -> " + str(malas))
    return filas


def prueba_3_grabaciones(d, filas):
    from clasifica import clave
    faltan = [f["id"] for f in filas
              if not (AQUI / "grabaciones" / (clave(f["texto"], d["modelo"]) + ".json")).exists()]
    ok = not faltan
    apunta(ok, "recordings: " + str(len(filas)) + " of " + str(len(filas)) + " emails have an answer"
           if ok else "recordings: missing for emails " + str(faltan) + " (run siembra.py)")


def prueba_4_demo_sin_red():
    original_socket = socket.socket
    original_conn = socket.create_connection
    argv = sys.argv[:]
    socket.socket = sin_red
    socket.create_connection = sin_red
    sys.argv = ["demo.py", "--rapido"]
    salida = io.StringIO()
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(salida):
            runpy.run_path(str(AQUI / "demo.py"), run_name="__main__")
        ok = "Correct:" in salida.getvalue()
        apunta(ok, "the demo runs with the network cut"
               if ok else "the demo ends without producing a result")
    except Exception as error:
        apunta(False, "the demo fails with the network cut -> " + str(error))
    finally:
        socket.socket = original_socket
        socket.create_connection = original_conn
        sys.argv = argv


def prueba_5_cifras(d):
    fichero = AQUI / "cifras.json"
    if not fichero.exists():
        apunta(False, "missing cifras.json (run: python cifras.py)")
        return
    c = json.loads(fichero.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ok = c["acierto"] >= d["acierto_prometido"]
    apunta(ok, "cifras.json: accuracy " + str(round(100 * c["acierto"], 1)) +
           " % (you promise " + str(round(100 * d["acierto_prometido"], 1)) + " %)")


def prueba_6_propuesta():
    fichero = AQUI / "PROPUESTA.md"
    if not fichero.exists():
        apunta(False, "missing PROPUESTA.md (run: python propuesta.py)")
        return
    texto = fichero.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    huecos = [m for m in ["XXX", "TODO", "[ ]", "pending definition"] if m in texto]
    ok = "EUR" in texto and "NOT include" in texto and not huecos
    apunta(ok, "PROPUESTA.md: " + str(len(texto)) + " characters, with price and no gaps"
           if ok else "PROPUESTA.md: problems -> " + str(huecos or "missing price or missing the 'does NOT include' section"))


def prueba_7_claves():
    # The pattern is split in two chunks so this very file doesn't trip it.
    pista = "sk-" + "ant-"
    sospechosos = []
    for f in AQUI.rglob("*"):
        if not f.is_file() or ".venv" in f.parts:
            continue
        if f.suffix in {".py", ".json", ".md", ".csv", ".txt", ".env"}:
            if pista in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                sospechosos.append(f.name)
    apunta(not sospechosos, "no key written anywhere in the project"
           if not sospechosos else "THERE IS A KEY WRITTEN in: " + ", ".join(sospechosos))


def main():
    print("")
    print("DRESS REHEARSAL - 7 checks")
    print("")
    d = prueba_1_datos()
    filas = prueba_2_correos()
    prueba_3_grabaciones(d, filas)
    prueba_4_demo_sin_red()
    prueba_5_cifras(d)
    prueba_6_propuesta()
    prueba_7_claves()

    for i, (ok, texto) in enumerate(resultados, 1):
        print(("[OK]   " if ok else "[FAIL]") + " " + str(i) + ". " + texto)

    print("")
    if all(ok for ok, _ in resultados):
        print("PACKAGE READY. You can show it.")
    else:
        print("Don't show it yet. Fix the [FAIL]s above.")
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: Seven lines in a row starting with `[OK]` and at the end "PACKAGE READY. You can show it." The fourth is the one that matters: "the demo runs with the network cut".
steps.trouble: If the fourth one shows `[FAIL] the demo fails with the network cut -> The demo tried to reach the internet`, you put something in demo.py that calls the model. Remove it: the demo only reads from `grabaciones/`. If you want a real call, that goes in a separate script.

steps.title: empaqueta.py: the README with the figures inside, and the zip
steps.why: The README is the first thing whoever receives the package opens, and it decides in twenty seconds whether they take you seriously. A script generates it so its numbers never go stale: measure again and the README updates itself. The zip excludes the virtual environment (which weighs 300 MB and is useless on another computer) and any `.env` file.
steps.code:
# empaqueta.py — writes the README and builds the zip you send.
'''Generates README.md and .gitignore, and compresses the project into entrega.zip.

The README carries the measured figures inside: measure again and it updates
itself. A README with stale numbers is worse than one with none.
'''
import json
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

AQUI = Path(__file__).parent
CARPETAS_FUERA = {".venv", "__pycache__", ".git", ".idea"}
ARCHIVOS_FUERA = {".env", "entrega.zip"}


def coma(numero, decimales=2):
    return ("{:." + str(decimales) + "f}").format(numero).replace(".", ",")


def escribe_readme(d, c):
    texto = rf'''# Incoming email classifier - {d["cliente"]}

Reads every incoming email and labels it: payroll, invoice, tax, meeting,
or other. Over {c["correos_probados"]} real emails it gets {c["aciertos"]} right ({coma(100 * c["acierto"], 1)} %).

## What you need

Python 3.11 or higher. Nothing else. **The demo needs no internet and no API
key**: the model's answers are recorded in the grabaciones/ folder.

## Getting it running (60 seconds)

    python -m venv .venv
    .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1        # Mac/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
    python siembra.py
    python demo.py

## What you'll see

A table of {c["correos_probados"]} rows: the trimmed email, the label the tool proposes, the
correct label, and OK or MISS. At the end:
"Correct: {c["aciertos"]} of {c["correos_probados"]}".

## The numbers

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Emails per month | {d["correos_al_mes"]} |
| By hand | {coma(c["horas_a_mano_mes"], 1)} h/month |
| With the tool | {coma(c["horas_con_herramienta_mes"], 1)} h/month |
| Hours saved | {coma(c["horas_ahorradas_mes"], 1)} h/month |
| Net savings | {coma(c["ahorro_neto_mes_eur"])} EUR/month |
| AI bill | {coma(c["coste_api_mes_eur"])} EUR/month |

The three commands that generate these numbers: siembra.py, demo.py, cifras.py.
Not a single number is typed by hand in this README.

## What it does NOT do

It doesn't reply to emails, doesn't read attachments, doesn't connect to
your accounting software, and doesn't get 100% right. It fails about
{coma(100 * (1 - c["acierto"]), 1)} % of the time and those emails have to be fixed by hand; that
time is already subtracted in the table above.

## The files

| File | What for |
| --- | --- |
| datos.json | All the project's numbers, in one place |
| siembra.py | Writes correos.csv and the example recordings |
| clasifica.py | The classifier. Replay mode and record mode |
| demo.py | The three-minute demo, no internet |
| cifras.py | Measures accuracy and turns it into hours and euros |
| propuesta.py | Generates PROPUESTA.md |
| verifica.py | Seven checks before showing anything |
| empaqueta.py | This README and the delivery zip |

## Recording real answers

The recordings shipped with the project are examples. With your own key:

    $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "your-key"     # Mac/Linux: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"
    python clasifica.py "an email's text" --grabar

Re-recording all {c["correos_probados"]} emails costs less than a cent with {d["modelo"]}.
The key is never written inside a file. If you write it in and push it to
GitHub, consider it burned: bots find them in under a minute.
'''
    (AQUI / "README.md").write_text(texto, encoding="utf-8")
    return len(texto)


def escribe_gitignore():
    (AQUI / ".gitignore").write_text(
        ".venv/\n.env\n__pycache__/\nentrega.zip\n", encoding="utf-8")


def monta_zip():
    destino = AQUI / "entrega.zip"
    metidos = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(destino, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for f in sorted(AQUI.rglob("*")):
            if not f.is_file():
                continue
            if set(f.relative_to(AQUI).parts) & CARPETAS_FUERA:
                continue
            if f.name in ARCHIVOS_FUERA:
                continue
            z.write(f, f.relative_to(AQUI))
            metidos += 1
    return destino, metidos


def main():
    d = json.loads((AQUI / "datos.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    fichero_cifras = AQUI / "cifras.json"
    if not fichero_cifras.exists():
        raise SystemExit("Missing cifras.json. Run first:  python cifras.py")
    c = json.loads(fichero_cifras.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    largo = escribe_readme(d, c)
    escribe_gitignore()
    destino, metidos = monta_zip()

    print("README.md written (" + str(largo) + " characters)")
    print(".gitignore written")
    print("entrega.zip: " + str(metidos) + " files, " +
          coma(destino.stat().st_size / 1024, 1) + " kB")
    print("")
    print("Before sending: open the zip and check what's inside. If .env,")
    print("a key, or an email with a client's real name shows up, delete")
    print("the zip and fix it. A file already sent can't be recalled.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: "README.md written", ".gitignore written", "entrega.zip: 25 files, about 20 kB" and the final warning. Open the zip and check: `.venv`, `.env`, or any key must not appear inside.
steps.trouble: If redirecting output to a file on Windows gives `UnicodeEncodeError`, run `$env:PYTHONUTF8 = "1"` before executing. It happens because the Windows console uses an old encoding for files; inside the code everything is already forced to UTF-8.

checks: You put the computer in airplane mode, run `python demo.py`, and the whole table finishes with not a single error.
`python verifica.py` gives seven `[OK]`s and "PACKAGE READY". If any fails, the package doesn't get shown.
No number is typed by hand twice: you search for `900` or `420` in the folder and they only show up in `datos.json`.
`PROPUESTA.md` has a section saying what it does NOT include. Without it, it isn't a proposal, it's a wish list.
You search for `sk-ant-` across the whole folder and it doesn't show up once. Not in the code, not in the zip, not in the recordings.
You hand `entrega.zip` to someone who's never seen the project, and in under five minutes they have the demo running just from the README, without asking you anything.
extend: Grow the sample from 12 to 50 emails. 91.7% over 12 emails has a huge margin of error; over 50 it's a number you can defend without sweating. Add rows to `siembra.py`'s list and run `python siembra.py --forzar`.

Have `propuesta.py` also generate an HTML version with a simple stylesheet, to print to PDF from the browser with Ctrl+P. No installs needed: the same information, with your brand's header and typeface.

Turn the €45/month maintenance into something visible: a script that each month reads the client's own labeled emails, recalculates accuracy, and writes a report. If accuracy drops below the 85% you promised, it alerts you. That way maintenance stops being a fee and becomes a service with proof.
defend: "What if there's no wifi on demo day?" — Nothing happens, because the demo doesn't use wifi. Every email turns into a unique fingerprint and its answer has been saved to disk since the day I recorded it. It comes out the same every time and takes four seconds. If the client asks whether that's cheating, I show them the recording file with its date and run `clasifica.py --grabar` live in front of them to re-record one, if there's network. A recorded demo isn't a trick: it's not betting the meeting on a room's wifi.

"Where does the 91.7% accuracy come from?" — From 11 correct out of 12 emails I labeled by hand, one by one. And that's exactly why I don't promise 91.7%: twelve emails is too few and the margin of error is large. In the proposal I commit to 85% measured over the client's first 100 real emails during the first week, and if I fall short I keep working for free or refund the implementation. Promising below what you measure is what lets you sleep.

"Why 900 euros? How do you justify it?" — Not by how many hours it costs me, by how much it saves them. It's 420 emails a month that at two minutes each eat up 14 hours; with the tool that drops to 3.5 hours, already counting the time to fix the 35 emails it'll get wrong. At 18 euros an hour that's 189 euros a month, minus 45 for maintenance and 6 cents of AI usage: 143.94 euros net. The 900 euros pay back in 6.3 months and the first year closes with 827 euros in their favor. If the client argues over price, we argue over the number that doesn't add up for them, not the price itself.
